As someone heavily involved in the discussion on PMF in Mathlib (but not a decision maker) I figured I would summarise some of the reasons the decision was made and further directions:

  1. Outside of use in do notation it doesnt make sense to design a whole API around PMF when one can simply use the linear combination of dirac masses or just include whatever assumptions are necessary. This is analogous to IsProbabilityMeasure. Unless one needs to use some structure on the space of probability measures one should just use the hypothesis to avoid duplicating API. There is however sometimes a need to use some structure on that space (for example the topology on Probability Measures) and in that case it is fine to use the ProbabilityMeasure type.

  2. do notation is a potential reason to want to use PMF since Measure is not a monad in the Lean core sense. However (from a Mathlib POV) carrying around the hypotheses that the PMF sums to one was unnecessary. You can simply add this hypotheses when needed. #34138 is developing a potential version of this. It was agreed that this would only be developed for use with do notation though and all definitions which can be defined more generally should be special cased to this when necessary (for example if one needs to define entropy for a DiscreteMeasure it should come from the measure definition).

  3. I agree that in principal it would be nice to allow people without measure theory background to use simple discrete probability downstream. I think this is very possible just with API improvements. Since the discussions started I believe me and @Etienne Marion have improved the situation by defining more theorems or simp lemmas that should make it easier to reduce from measure theoretic definitions immediately to the discrete special case. Definitely a lot more work to do here though.

  4. One potential long term direction is to make do notation work for the Giry Monad. This is not compatible with core lean do notation because Measure needs a measure space argument but if you simply define a new "random_do" notation where you copy everything in core lean but add a measure space type class argument you can make it work. I have working prototype that allows you to define probabilistic algorithms and even in a polymorphic way so that one can interpret them using Measure or the Rand monad (to run the program with a psuedorandom number generator). However there are definitely issues, for example one would expect that most of the regular do notation functionality works (such as apply Monad transformers which I imagine is important for CSLib) and making it feasible to prove things (probably needs some good custom automation). I think its doable but needs lots of work. Perhaps Eric's suggestion is an alternative.

This is a really important point, which I want to emphasise. I'm someone who cares about discrete probability primarily in the finite, discrete setting, particularly because of formalising combinatorics and TCS. And so for quite a while, I viewed Mathlib's measure theory as being far too heavy and distracting for what I actually care about (and this is as someone who knows enough measure theory to know it's heavy!). But my opinion has switched completely now, and I'm now strongly of the opinion that this special case is significantly cleaner to use. However as David says, it's not perfect, and the ideal situation is that in the finite discrete case it's very easy to move between the measure theory world and the finite weighted sums world, which isn't as easy as it should be (it's possible, and getting easier, but not there yet). But for me, the real benefit is that results from general probability theory (eg the Chernoff bound) are things which are a lot less nice to state and prove in terms of PMFs, but we're in the much more convenient world where I can specialise it easily to my finite discrete random variable (in the mathlib sense), and it all works nicely.
For this reason, PMF has been "discouraged" in mathlib for a little while, but note that it hasn't yet been actually deprecated - this is in large part because it's not yet as convenient as we'd like to take this (important, at least to me) special case, and Etienne and David are fixing this. I expect PMF won't be formally deprecated until this alternative is friendlier to people who don't want to learn measure theory: but mathlib cares about making sure these people can still reap the benefits of measure theory.

It does feel to me that this would be a great opportunity to develop a more lightweight theory of probability that doesn't use measure theory.

Jones and Plotkin 89 "a probabilistic powerdomain of evaluations"
If you ever want to do Hoare triples, that is basically the canonical setup
(or to rephrase, if you ever want to do fixpoints, that is basically the canonical setup)
The choice of [0,1] vs ENNReal is mostly deferrable, but you want "functions over open sets that take directed unions to suprema"

you then get a Hoare type logic of triples

Judgement (X →sc ℝ≥0∞) (X →sc (Opens Y) →sc ℝ≥0∞) (Y →sc ℝ≥0∞) : Prop

where →sc denotes Scott-continuous functions. And this is compatible with the measure space formulation
And you get all your usual loop invariant etc fixpoints rules, chain completeness (and equivalence given Choice), lifting of standard monadic triple rules
(I am eliding some linearity laws here, eg sums of disjoint subsets)
But it works exactly as you'd want it to for discrete spaces, and then has enough nice fixpoints for modelling interaction etc

and because the derivation comes from the WP semantics point of view, it's well oriented for managing the abstraction between properties (e.g. satisfaction probability, expected value, correctness..... Bayesian likelihood ratios if you're into those) vs small-step behaviours

Sorry for having missed this thread, I PRed #34138 with DiscreteMeasure to Mathlib. Improvements I intend here:

  • The PMF has the HasSum 1 property bundled in, and in mathematics, I would also like to reason about measures which do not sum to one.
  • Since the measure theory API in mathlib is built very well, code should not be duplicated for the discrete measures, but the available measure theory code should be used. I do this mostly by saying that the underlying measurable space is the full power set. (Therefore, there is no need to think about measurable spaces if only discrete measures are involved.)
  • I really like do notation, and I would like to reason about it. (Using do-notation is not common in mathlib, as I understand.) Therefore, there will be a LawfulMonad DiscreteMeasure instance. (For example, for having a recursive definition of the binomial distribution, arguing that this is the same by counting successes of coins and showing the classical binomial formula.)
How does the proposed DiscreteMeasurecompare to docs#StdSimplex ? Nevermind, StdSimplex is closer to PMF with the integral-one condition.

I do like the idea of not needing separate PMF and SPMF types that this would give us as well, instead just assuming appropriate hypotheses about the sum. In particular it seems writing p >>= q would let you keep the PMF-analogue when both are sum 1, and still have the SPMF-analogue instance when one of the two is only a sum < 1
Although I don't think mathlib currently has a sub-probability measure version of IsProbabilityMeasure
